package_info.why_malicious: Vulnerable versions of these packages do not properly restrict XML External Entity (XXE) processing. This allows attackers to inject malicious XML payloads that can access local files, perform server-side request forgery (SSRF), or cause denial of service (DoS) by exploiting the XML parser's entity expansion capabilities. The risk is especially high when user-supplied XML is parsed without secure configuration, leading to potential data exfiltration or system compromise.

execution_context.file_location: Any Java class or method that parses XML input using DocumentBuilderFactory, XMLInputFactory, or similar XML parsing utilities without secure configuration
required_permissions: filesystem (to read local files referenced by external entities)
network (if SYSTEM entities reference remote resources)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This XML payload defines an external entity 'xxe' that references the local file /etc/passwd. When a vulnerable XML parser processes this input, it expands the 'xxe' entity and includes the contents of /etc/passwd in the parsed XML data. This can result in sensitive file disclosure if the application returns or processes the expanded data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of a SYSTEM external entity referencing a sensitive file in user-supplied XML is a classic XXE attack vector. This technique is used to exfiltrate sensitive files or trigger SSRF/DoS via entity expansion.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Secure XML processing should not allow user-supplied XML to define or expand external entities that access local files or remote resources. The parser should have external entity resolution and DTD processing disabled.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: External entities can be used in trusted, internal XML DTDs for modularization or referencing shared resources, but should never be allowed in untrusted or user-supplied XML, especially when referencing sensitive files or external URLs.
key_indicators: User-supplied XML containing a DOCTYPE declaration with SYSTEM entity references
Entity definitions referencing local files (e.g., file:///etc/passwd) or remote URLs
Expansion of user-controlled entities during XML parsing

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when Java code parses XML input)
execution_context.file_location: Java code that instantiates and uses DocumentBuilderFactory, XMLInputFactory, or similar XML parser classes without explicitly disabling external entity resolution or DTD processing

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This Java code creates a DocumentBuilderFactory and parses XML input without setting secure features to disable external entity resolution or DTD processing. If the input is attacker-controlled, this code is vulnerable to XXE attacks, allowing attackers to access local files or trigger SSRF via crafted XML.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code does not set any features to disable external entity resolution or DTD processing, leaving the parser vulnerable to XXE attacks when parsing untrusted XML input.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Secure XML parsing requires explicit disabling of external entity resolution (e.g., setFeature("http://xml.org/sax/features/external-general-entities", false)) and DTD processing. Omitting these settings exposes the application to XXE risks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Parsing static, trusted XML files may not require these protections, but any code that processes user-supplied or dynamic XML must enforce secure parser configuration to prevent XXE.
key_indicators: Java code using DocumentBuilderFactory, XMLInputFactory, or similar without calls to setFeature to disable external entities and DTDs
No explicit disabling of external entity resolution or DTD processing in parser configuration
Parsing of XML input that may be controlled by external users

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits a malicious XML payload containing a DOCTYPE declaration with an external entity referencing a sensitive file or remote resource.
attack_chain.leads_to: The XML parser receives and begins processing the crafted input.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable XML parser (e.g., DocumentBuilderFactory) processes the XML without restricting external entity resolution or DTD processing.
attack_chain.leads_to: The parser expands the external entity, accessing the referenced file or making a network request.

attack_chain.action: The contents of the referenced file or the result of the network request are included in the application's XML processing result, which may be returned to the attacker or used in further processing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is exfiltrated, SSRF is performed, or denial of service occurs, depending on the attacker's payload.

behavioral_signatures: User-supplied XML input containing DOCTYPE declarations with SYSTEM entity references
Unexpected file system or network access during XML parsing operations
Expansion of user-controlled XML entities in application logs or output
file_indicators: XML files or payloads with <!DOCTYPE ... [ <!ENTITY ... SYSTEM ...> ]> patterns
Java source code using DocumentBuilderFactory, XMLInputFactory, or similar without secure parser configuration (e.g., missing setFeature calls to disable external entities and DTDs)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to attacker-controlled domains or IPs during XML parsing
Unexpected access to internal network resources (SSRF) triggered by XML entity expansion
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor XML parsing operations for the presence of DOCTYPE declarations and SYSTEM entity references in user-supplied XML. Use static code analysis to identify Java code that instantiates XML parsers without disabling external entity resolution and DTD processing. Monitor application logs and system calls for unexpected file or network access during XML processing. Flag any XML input or code paths that allow user-controlled entity expansion.
